question.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x={a}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘},\,x={210}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
question.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2} & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2} & ={315}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘} & \, & \, & 3x & ={630}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={210}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=30.$
